title: GST 111 (COOU) | Chapter Seven: Parts of Speech
subject: GST 111

questions.question: A word in English can belong to more than one part of speech depending on its?
questions.explanation: A word can belong to more than one part of speech depending on its function in a sentence.

questions.question: In 'The FAST has begun', the word FAST is a?
questions.explanation: In this sentence FAST functions as a noun.

questions.question: In 'Kamsi bought a FAST car', the word FAST is an?
questions.explanation: In this sentence FAST qualifies the noun car, so it is an adjective.

questions.question: In 'Peter is FASTING', the word FASTING is a?
questions.explanation: In this sentence FASTING expresses an action, so it is a verb.

questions.question: In 'The car is moving FAST', the word FAST is an?
questions.explanation: In this sentence FAST modifies the verb moving, so it is an adverb.

questions.question: A noun has been defined traditionally as a name of a person, place, thing, state, activity or?
questions.explanation: A noun is a name of a person, place, thing, state, activity or quantity.

questions.question: Proper nouns are particular names given to a particular person, place, thing, days in the week and?
questions.explanation: Proper nouns include names of days in the week and names of the month in the year.

questions.question: A proper noun must begin with a capital letter anywhere it appears in a?
questions.explanation: A proper noun must begin with a capital letter anywhere it appears in a sentence.

questions.question: Proper nouns are not preceded by a definite or an?
questions.explanation: Proper nouns are not preceded by a definite or an indefinite article.

questions.question: Common nouns are names given to people or things of the same?
questions.explanation: Common nouns are names given to people or things of the same class.

questions.question: Abstract nouns name state, quality or?
questions.explanation: Abstract nouns name state, quality or action.

questions.question: Abstract nouns name those things that cannot be seen or?
questions.explanation: Abstract nouns name things that cannot be seen or touched.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of an abstract noun?
questions.explanation: Happiness is an example of an abstract noun listed in the chapter.

questions.question: Collective nouns are names given to a group of persons or things taken to be a?
questions.explanation: Collective nouns are names given to a group of persons or things taken to be a whole.

questions.question: Which of these is a collective noun?
questions.explanation: Parliament is listed as an example of a collective noun.

questions.question: Countable nouns can accept the articles 'a' or 'an' before them and can also be?
questions.explanation: Countable nouns can accept articles and can also be pluralized.

questions.question: Uncountable nouns are used with 'much' or?
questions.explanation: Uncountable nouns are used with much or little.

questions.question: Which of these is an uncountable noun?
questions.explanation: Air is listed as an example of an uncountable noun.

questions.question: Traditional Grammar defines a verb as a doing word or an ______ word in a sentence.
questions.explanation: A verb is defined as a doing word or an action word in a sentence.

questions.question: Come, eat, sleep and jump are described in the chapter as?
questions.explanation: The text states that these words are sentences with implied subjects.

questions.question: A verb is said to be finite when it reflects number, person, tense and?
questions.explanation: A finite verb reflects number, person, tense and mood.

questions.question: Lexical verbs can also be called?
questions.explanation: Lexical verbs can also be called main verbs.

questions.question: A transitive verb must have an?
questions.explanation: A transitive verb must have an object.

questions.question: Intransitive verbs do not transfer the action of the verb to any?
questions.explanation: Intransitive verbs do not transfer the action to any object.

questions.question: Auxiliary verbs help the main verbs to form their tenses and perform their?
questions.explanation: Auxiliary verbs help main verbs form tenses and perform their functions.

questions.question: The primary auxiliaries are have, do and?
questions.explanation: The primary auxiliaries are have, do and be.

questions.question: Modal auxiliaries include shall, will, may, might, would, can, could and?
questions.explanation: Modal auxiliaries include shall, will, may, might, would, can, could and should.

questions.question: The full infinitives are preceded by?
questions.explanation: Full infinitives are preceded by 'to'.

questions.question: The gerund is the type of a verb that ends in?
questions.explanation: The gerund ends in -ing and can be used as a noun.

questions.question: A participle is in form of a verb that functions like an?
questions.explanation: A participle functions like an adjective.

questions.question: Past participle ends with the past tense marker?
questions.explanation: Past participle ends with the past tense marker -ed.

questions.question: An adjective is a word that qualifies as well as ______ a noun.
questions.explanation: An adjective qualifies as well as quantifies a noun.

questions.question: Possessive adjectives indicate ownership or?
questions.explanation: Possessive adjectives indicate ownership or possession.

questions.question: Demonstrative adjectives point at person or things they are?
questions.explanation: Demonstrative adjectives point at the person or things they refer to.

questions.question: Descriptive adjectives are used to ______ the nouns they qualify.
questions.explanation: Descriptive adjectives are used to describe the nouns they qualify.

questions.question: Distributive adjectives are used to refer to each and every person?
questions.explanation: Distributive adjectives refer to each and every person separately.

questions.question: Interrogative adjectives are used to ask?
questions.explanation: Interrogative adjectives are used to ask questions.

questions.question: Emphasizing adjectives are used to lay ______ on the nouns they qualify.
questions.explanation: Emphasizing adjectives lay emphasis on the nouns they qualify.

questions.question: Indefinite adjectives do not give the ______ number of the nouns they qualify.
questions.explanation: Indefinite adjectives do not give the exact number of the nouns they qualify.

questions.question: Numerical adjectives deal with the ______ number.
questions.explanation: Numerical adjectives deal with the exact number.

questions.question: An adverb is a word that modifies a verb, an adjective or another?
questions.explanation: An adverb modifies a verb, an adjective or another adverb.

questions.question: Adjuncts give additional information to the sentences where they?
questions.explanation: Adjuncts give additional information to the sentences where they occur.

questions.question: Adverbs of time show the ______ of an action.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of time show the time of an action.

questions.question: Adverbs of place indicate the ______ of an action.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of place indicate the place of an action.

questions.question: Adverbs of manner tell the ______ with which an action happens.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of manner tell the manner with which an action happens.

questions.question: Adverbs of degree show the degree or to what ______ an action is done.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of degree show to what extent an action is done.

questions.question: Adverbs of frequency show how ______ an action takes place.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency show how often an action takes place.

questions.question: Disjuncts show the ______ of the speaker towards a given sentence.
questions.explanation: Disjuncts show the attitude of the speaker towards a given sentence.

questions.question: Conjuncts are linking adverbs used to link a?
questions.explanation: Conjuncts are linking adverbs used to link a paragraph.

questions.question: A pronoun is a word that ______ a noun in a sentence.
questions.explanation: A pronoun is a word that replaces a noun in a sentence.
